provenance: Authored against the sponsor's BDM scope (CAR-T for LN, CAR-T for MS, Long-Term Follow-Up). Calibrated to demonstrate value-add operational levers the sponsor's payor data plan cares about — completeness, retention, data purity — without inflating cost or speed-to-data on the main study.

section.headline: Four LTFU questions that move payor-grade data, not just patient counts.
section.body: Sponsor priorities sit at speed and cost to main-study readout. The award-defining differentiation likely sits in the LTFU tail. Each question below pairs evidence we could source from patients with a concrete operational intervention the BDM can frame as low-cost, high-completeness.

questions.label: What keeps patients tethered to LTFU when CAR-T feels like a cure?
questions.summary: By year 3, biology is stable and the rationale for trial-site visits fades. Retention requires a low-burden touch model that earns its keep year over year.

research.headline: Questions to ask or source from patients
items: At year 3 vs year 8, what makes a phone or video LTFU check feel like care vs surveillance?
Which labs and PROs are patients willing to do quarterly from home for a decade, and which feel like overreach?
What digital touchpoint cadence (text, app, portal, telehealth) keeps patients engaged without feeling tracked?
What would make a local lab draw feel official enough to count, not like a shortcut?

items.label: The Digital Tether framework
items.body: Years 3–12 do not require expensive site visits. Stand up a digital-first LTFU spine: telehealth check-ins, contracted local-lab blood draws, ePRO for fatigue / kidney symptoms / steroid-free flare days. Frames the BDM as ultra-low cost without trading away completeness.

items.label: Tiered visit ladder
items.body: Annual in-person window for years 1–2, then alternating telehealth + local-lab quarters from year 3 onward, with an in-person reset every 3 years. Lets sites flex staffing to acute-window patients.

questions.label: Where do site-to-community handoffs break the 12-year horizon?
questions.summary: By year 5, original PI may have moved on and the LN patient's rheumatology / nephrology dyad is owned by community providers. Without them as protocol allies, retention bleeds.

research.headline: Questions to ask or source from patients
items: Who is the patient's call-first provider at year 1, year 5, year 10? Does the trial site stay on that list?
What does a community rheumatologist / nephrologist need to feel ownership of LTFU data, not just an annual form?
What does the patient hear from their community team when a CAR-T history appears in the chart five years later?
When PI rotation happens, what would make the patient stay vs drop out?

items.label: Site-to-community transition bundles
items.body: Position the team as authors of transition kits for community rheumatology and nephrology. Includes a one-pager on the 12-year data thesis, an LTFU visit checklist, a flare-management protocol that does not confound efficacy data, and a direct-line escalation contact.

items.label: PI-rotation continuity plan
items.body: Pre-commit to a named continuity contact (study coordinator role, not the original PI) that the patient meets in year 1 and persists through PI churn. Removes the who-do-I-call-if-I-have-a-blip-in-2038 risk.

questions.label: How do we detect off-protocol immunosuppression before it confounds efficacy?
questions.summary: B-cell depleting therapies are the default for LN flare. Without an early-warning system, community providers will reach for them at the first symptom, contaminating the durability signal payors care about.

research.headline: Questions to ask or source from patients
items: At first symptom that feels like a flare, who does the patient call first — trial site, community rheum, ER?
What rescue-therapy reasoning do community providers cite when bringing patients back onto B-cell depleters?
What patient-facing materials would the patient share with a community provider to pause the rescue conversation?
What does the patient consider an acceptable trade-off between symptom relief and trial-protocol fidelity?

items.label: Early-warning system for rescue immunosuppression
items.body: Build LTFU tracking that flags any new immunosuppressive prescription within 30 days, with a structured ascertainment workflow. Catches the rescue-therapy decision before it becomes a year-of-data loss.

items.label: Patient-held rescue-decision protocol
items.body: Give patients a one-page rescue-decision card to bring to community-provider visits — when to call the site first, when a non-confounding bridge therapy is appropriate, when rescue is the right call. Aligns the patient as an active partner in protocol fidelity.

questions.label: Which payor-grade evidence matters in years 5–12, and how do we collect it without burning patients out?
questions.summary: Payors will price the durability of an autoimmune CAR-T against rituximab-cycle costs avoided, steroid-free interval, and work productivity recovered. None of those live in the main-study CRF.

research.headline: Questions to ask or source from patients
items: What does work / school / caregiving look like for the patient at year 3, year 5, year 10 post-infusion?
What out-of-pocket costs continue (or end) once the patient is off immunosuppression?
What does a steroid-free year vs a steroid-touched year feel like in the patient's own framing?
Which life events (pregnancy attempt, surgery, infection, vaccine) would the patient flag as worth a longitudinal data point?

items.label: Payor-aligned ePRO bank
items.body: Curate a short ePRO bank — work-productivity, steroid-burden, healthcare-utilization avoidance — surfaced quarterly at near-zero patient burden. Generates exactly the cost-offset narrative payors will demand at launch.

items.label: Life-event capture micro-survey
items.body: A 2-minute patient-initiated capture for the events that drive payor questions (pregnancy, surgery, infection, vaccine). Catches the longitudinal signal that quarterly visits miss.
